items.q: Look! The cat ______ on the kitchen table again.
items.vi: Nhìn kìa! Con mèo lại đang ngủ trên bàn bếp.
items.explanation: Present continuous for an action happening now: Look! tells us the cat is on the table at this moment, so is sleeping fits. ✗ sleeps — present simple is for habits, not what we can see as we speak; ✗ slept — past simple puts the action in the finished past; ✗ has slept — present perfect reports a completed action, not one in progress.

items.q: The kitten ______ its paw on a piece of broken glass in the garden.
items.vi: Con mèo con bị đứt chân vì một mảnh thủy tinh vỡ trong vườn.
items.explanation: Word choice for injuries: broken glass has a sharp edge, so it makes a cut (an opening in the skin). ✗ bruised — a bruise is a dark mark from a knock, not from a sharp edge; ✗ sprained — you sprain a joint by twisting it; ✗ strained — you strain a muscle by overusing it. Neither comes from glass.

items.q: Everyone expects Tuan's dog to ______ at Sunday's race because it is much faster than the others.
items.vi: Ai cũng nghĩ chó của Tuấn sẽ thắng dễ dàng ở cuộc đua hôm Chủ nhật vì nó nhanh hơn hẳn những con khác.
items.explanation: Idiom for winning: much faster than the others means an easy victory, so win hands down (win very easily) fits. ✗ run out of steam — lose energy and slow down; ✗ win by a whisker — win by a tiny margin, the opposite of an easy win; ✗ lose its way — go in the wrong direction, so no win at all.

items.q: You should ______ your promise to visit Grandma this weekend, or she will be very upset.
items.vi: Con nên giữ lời hứa đi thăm bà vào cuối tuần này, không thì bà sẽ buồn lắm.
items.explanation: Collocation with promise: the fixed verb is keep a promise (do what you said you would), and or she will be very upset shows that breaking it is the danger. ✗ hold — you hold a meeting or hold on, not a promise; ✗ stay — cannot take 'promise' as an object; ✗ save — you save money or time, not a promise.

items.q: Don't ______ your teammates by missing the school cooking contest on Saturday.
items.vi: Đừng làm đồng đội thất vọng bằng cách bỏ lỡ cuộc thi nấu ăn của trường vào thứ Bảy.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: let somebody down = disappoint someone, which is what missing the contest would do to teammates. ✗ turn down — refuse an offer or request, not something you do to people who rely on you; ✗ let off — not punish someone; ✗ put down — criticise someone, or place something on a surface.

items.q: Nobody could explain the reason ______ the school swimming pool stayed closed all summer.
items.vi: Không ai giải thích được lý do vì sao bể bơi của trường đóng cửa suốt cả mùa hè.
items.explanation: Relative adverb after the reason: the fixed pattern is the reason why + clause. ✗ which — a relative pronoun must be the subject or object of its clause, but 'the pool stayed closed' already has its subject and needs no object; ✗ where — follows a place noun; ✗ when — follows a time noun.

items.q: After eating the fish that had been left out in the sun, Nam felt ______ and had to lie down.
items.vi: Sau khi ăn con cá bị để ngoài nắng, Nam thấy buồn nôn và phải nằm nghỉ.
items.explanation: Word choice for illness: fish left out in the sun gives you food poisoning, so Nam felt sick (ill, wanting to vomit). ✗ sore — a body part is sore (painful), not the whole person after bad food; ✗ bruised — marked by a knock; ✗ hurt — injured, or emotionally upset, not ill.

items.q: The bowl is empty — the cat ______ all the fish while we were out.
items.vi: Cái bát trống không — chắc chắn con mèo đã ăn hết cá lúc chúng ta đi vắng.
items.explanation: Modal of past deduction: the bowl is empty is the evidence, so must have eaten (I'm sure it happened) fits. ✗ can't have eaten — the opposite deduction (I'm sure it didn't), contradicted by the empty bowl; ✗ should have eaten — criticises something that did not happen; ✗ needn't have eaten — it happened but was unnecessary; neither is a guess from evidence.

items.q: Parrots are famous ______ copying the sounds of human speech.
items.vi: Vẹt nổi tiếng vì bắt chước được âm thanh tiếng người.
items.explanation: Adjective + preposition: famous for + the thing someone is known for (copying human speech). ✗ of — 'famous of' does not exist (compare 'proud of'); ✗ about — 'famous about' does not exist (compare 'worried about'); ✗ with — 'famous with' is not used (compare 'popular with').

items.q: My grandmother ______ the same soup recipe since she was a little girl.
items.vi: Bà tôi đã dùng cùng một công thức nấu canh này từ khi bà còn là một cô bé.
items.explanation: Present perfect with since: since she was a little girl marks the start of a period that continues to now, so has used fits. ✗ uses — present simple gives a habit but cannot combine with a 'since' starting point; ✗ used — past simple would mean she has stopped; ✗ is using — present continuous is for right now, not a period from childhood.

items.q: Lan's ankle became ______ after she twisted it on the mountain trail.
items.vi: Cổ chân của Lan bị sưng lên sau khi cô ấy bị trẹo chân trên đường mòn lên núi.
items.explanation: Word choice for a body part: a twisted ankle becomes swollen (bigger than normal). ✗ dizzy — a person feels dizzy (the room spins), not an ankle; ✗ hoarse — describes a rough, tired voice; ✗ feverish — describes a person with a high temperature.

items.q: Could you ______ the table while I finish the spring rolls?
items.vi: Con dọn bàn ăn giúp mẹ trong lúc mẹ làm nốt chả giò được không?
items.explanation: Collocation: lay the table = put out the plates and chopsticks before a meal, the clue being while I finish the spring rolls. ✗ put — needs a place ('put the plates on the table'); ✗ make — you make a table only if you build it; ✗ do — 'do the table' is not a collocation (we do the dishes, the washing-up).

items.q: Lan: Are we going to the beach tomorrow? / Nam: If the weather ______ fine, we'll take the dog with us.
items.vi: Lan: Mai mình đi biển chứ? / Nam: Nếu trời đẹp, mình sẽ dắt chó theo.
items.explanation: First conditional: tomorrow and we'll take in the main clause show a real future condition, so the if-clause takes the present simple is. ✗ will be — 'will' is not used in the if-clause of a first conditional; ✗ was — past simple makes an unreal second conditional, which needs 'would' in the main clause; ✗ would be — 'would' belongs in the main clause, not after 'if'.

items.q: Planting ten trees is only ______ when a whole forest has been cut down.
items.vi: Trồng mười cái cây chỉ như muối bỏ biển khi cả một khu rừng đã bị chặt.
items.explanation: Idiom: ten trees against a whole forest is a tiny amount compared with what is needed — a drop in the ocean. ✗ a piece of cake — something very easy; ✗ a storm in a teacup — a big fuss about something unimportant; ✗ a breath of fresh air — something pleasantly new and different.

items.q: There is only ______ rice left in the pot, so I'll cook some noodles as well.
items.vi: Trong nồi chỉ còn một ít cơm, nên mình sẽ nấu thêm mì.
items.explanation: Quantifier with an uncountable noun: rice has no plural, so a little (a small amount) fits, and only confirms it is a small amount. ✗ a few — only with plural countable nouns (a few grains); ✗ many — plural countable only, and means a lot, clashing with 'only'; ✗ several — plural countable only.

items.q: Mai has a bad ______, so she keeps coughing and sneezing in class.
items.vi: Mai bị cảm nặng nên cứ ho và hắt hơi liên tục trong lớp.
items.explanation: Word choice for illness: coughing and sneezing are the symptoms of a cold. ✗ ache — a dull continuous pain, as in backache; ✗ bruise — a dark mark on the skin after a knock; ✗ rash — a patch of red spots on the skin. None of these makes you cough or sneeze.

items.q: Our old dog ______ peacefully last winter, and we buried him under the mango tree.
items.vi: Con chó già của chúng tôi đã qua đời thanh thản vào mùa đông năm ngoái, và chúng tôi chôn nó dưới gốc xoài.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: passed away is the gentle word for died, matching we buried him. ✗ passed out — fainted, lost consciousness; ✗ gave away — gave something to someone for free, and needs an object; ✗ passed by — went past a place.

items.q: The vet said she ______ the problem with our rabbit's teeth the next day.
items.vi: Bác sĩ thú y nói rằng hôm sau cô ấy sẽ xem xét vấn đề về răng của con thỏ nhà chúng tôi.
items.explanation: Reported speech backshift: after said, and with the next day (reported 'tomorrow'), will becomes would look into. ✗ will look into — no backshift after a past reporting verb; ✗ looks into — present simple does not report a future plan; ✗ has looked into — present perfect clashes with 'said' and with 'the next day'.

items.q: Nam: Shall we eat out tonight? / Lan: I'd rather ______ at home; I've bought some fresh prawns.
items.vi: Nam: Tối nay mình ra ngoài ăn nhé? / Lan: Tớ thích nấu ở nhà hơn; tớ mới mua ít tôm tươi.
items.explanation: Verb form after would rather: it takes the bare infinitive, so I'd rather cook. ✗ cooking — the -ing form follows 'prefer', not 'would rather'; ✗ to cook — 'to' follows 'would prefer', not 'would rather'; ✗ cooked — a past form makes no sense after 'rather' for tonight's plan.

items.q: When I got home from school, my dog ______ my new slippers to pieces.
items.vi: Khi tôi đi học về thì con chó đã cắn nát đôi dép mới của tôi.
items.explanation: Past perfect for the earlier of two past actions: When I got home is past simple, and the chewing happened before that, so had chewed. ✗ chews — present simple cannot follow a past time clause; ✗ has chewed — present perfect links to now, not to a past moment; ✗ is chewing — present continuous is for right now, not last afternoon.

items.q: Minh has a terrible ______, so he can't chew the sticky rice cake his mother made.
items.vi: Minh bị đau răng dữ dội nên không nhai được bánh chưng mẹ làm.
items.explanation: Word choice for pains: can't chew points to the mouth, so toothache. ✗ headache — pain in the head, which does not stop you chewing; ✗ earache — pain in the ear; ✗ stomachache — pain in the stomach, which might stop you eating but not chewing.

items.q: Nam loves spicy food, ______ his sister cannot eat even a little chilli.
items.vi: Nam rất thích đồ ăn cay, trong khi chị của cậu ấy không ăn nổi dù chỉ một chút ớt.
items.explanation: Linking word of contrast: loves spicy food and cannot eat even a little chilli are opposites, so whereas. ✗ therefore — introduces a result, and needs a full stop or semicolon before it; ✗ so that — introduces a purpose; ✗ because — gives a reason, but her dislike is not the cause of his love.

items.q: Fresh vegetables ______ to the market every morning by farmers from the countryside.
items.vi: Rau tươi được nông dân từ vùng quê chở đến chợ mỗi sáng.
items.explanation: Present simple passive: the subject vegetables receives the action and by farmers names the agent, so are brought; every morning makes it present simple. ✗ bring — active, but vegetables cannot bring themselves; ✗ brought — past simple active, wrong voice and clashes with 'every morning'; ✗ are bringing — active continuous, wrong voice.

items.q: Lan: Why don't you buy frozen fish? It's cheaper. / Nam: Fresh fish tastes far ______ than frozen fish.
items.vi: Lan: Sao cậu không mua cá đông lạnh? Rẻ hơn mà. / Nam: Cá tươi ăn ngon hơn cá đông lạnh nhiều.
items.explanation: Comparative: than requires a comparative, and the irregular comparative of good is better; far strengthens it. ✗ best — superlative, used with 'the', not 'than'; ✗ good — base form cannot go with 'than'; ✗ well — an adverb, but 'tastes' is a linking verb that takes an adjective, and it is not comparative anyway.

items.q: After dinner, Nam always ______ the washing-up so that his mother can rest.
items.vi: Sau bữa tối, Nam luôn rửa bát để mẹ được nghỉ ngơi.
items.explanation: Collocation: do the washing-up (wash the dishes), like do the cooking or do the dishes. ✗ makes — 'make' creates something (make a cake), not a chore; ✗ takes — you take a shower or a break, not the washing-up; ✗ gets — 'get the washing-up' would mean fetch it, not do it.
